entry.title: The room changes as they move
entry.summary: As a baby reaches farther or begins to crawl, the authors describe adapting the space to what is now reachable, with hazards removed or secured and stable supports for self-initiated pulling up.
entry.cue: Your baby can reach, open or lean on something that was out of reach before.
detail: Their “yes space,” a term they credit to Magda Gerber and RIE, is an area prepared around what the baby can actually do. They describe secure furniture, inaccessible cords and chemicals, and objects suitable for mouthing.
One adapted area can serve a family; the whole home need not be transformed at once. Low, heavy furniture appears among their examples once the baby begins pulling up.
